title: Create a Low‑Calorie Veggie Pasta with Zucchini Noodles
meta_description: Learn how to make a low‑calorie veggie pasta using mandoline zucchini noodles pasta, plus tips for perfect ribbons with a Mandoline Slicer.
html:
Swapping traditional wheat spaghetti for fresh mandoline zucchini noodles pasta can shave off calories while adding a bright crunch to your dinner plate. With a good Mandoline Slicer, you’ll get uniform, restaurant‑thin ribbons in seconds, making the whole process feel like a professional kitchen hack.

Why Choose Zucchini Noodles for a Low‑Calorie Meal

Zucchini is naturally low in carbs—about 3 grams per cup—and packed with vitamin C, potassium, and antioxidants. When you turn it into noodles, you keep the fiber that helps you feel full longer, while dramatically reducing the calorie count compared with a typical pasta dish. The mild flavor also lets you experiment with bold sauces without overwhelming the palate.

Getting Perfect Ribbons with a Mandoline Slicer

Achieving consistent, thin noodles is the biggest challenge for most home cooks. A quality Mandoline Slicer solves that problem. Its adjustable blades let you set the thickness from 1 mm up to 5 mm, and the built‑in hand guard keeps your fingers safe while you glide the zucchini across the blade. The result? Even, restaurant‑thin ribbons that cook evenly and hold sauce beautifully.

Step‑by‑Step: Making Mandoline Zucchini Noodles Pasta

  1. Prep the zucchini. Wash 2–3 medium zucchinis and trim the ends. If the skin is thick, you can peel it, but the skin adds color and nutrients, so leave it on unless you prefer a smoother noodle.
  2. Slice with the Mandoline Slicer. Set the blade to the thinnest setting you like—typically 1‑2 mm for a spaghetti‑like texture. Use the hand guard and slide the zucchini lengthwise, collecting the ribbons on a clean kitchen towel.
  3. Remove excess moisture. Place the ribbons in a colander, sprinkle lightly with salt, and let sit for 10 minutes. The salt draws out water, preventing a soggy final dish.
  4. Pat dry. After the zucchini has released its moisture, gently pat the noodles with paper towels. This step is crucial for achieving a slight bite when you sauté them.
  5. Sauté briefly. Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the noodles and toss for 2–3 minutes, just until they warm through and develop a hint of color. Overcooking will make them mushy.
  6. Combine with sauce. Toss the hot noodles with your favorite low‑calorie sauce—think a simple garlic‑olive oil blend, fresh tomato basil, or a light pesto made with basil, lemon, and a touch of Parmesan.
  7. Serve and garnish. Finish with a sprinkle of fresh herbs, a grind of black pepper, or a handful of toasted pine nuts for crunch.

Low‑Calorie Sauce Ideas that Pair Perfectly

Because zucchini noodles absorb flavors quickly, you can keep the sauce light and still enjoy a satisfying meal. Here are three go‑to options:

  • Garlic‑Lemon Olive Oil. Sauté minced garlic in olive oil, add a splash of lemon juice, and finish with chopped parsley.
  • Fresh Tomato Basil. Cook diced tomatoes with garlic, basil, and a pinch of red pepper flakes until saucy.
  • Green Avocado Pesto. Blend ripe avocado, basil, garlic, lemon juice, and a drizzle of olive oil for a creamy, low‑fat pesto.

Storing and Reheating Your Zucchini Noodles

If you have leftovers, store the noodles and sauce separately in airtight containers in the fridge for up to 3 days. To reheat, quickly toss the noodles in a hot skillet with a splash of water or broth; avoid microwaving as it can make them watery.

Tips for Success and Common Mistakes to Avoid

Don’t over‑salt. While the initial salting helps draw out moisture, too much can make the noodles salty. Rinse briefly if you’re concerned.

Use the right blade setting. Thinner blades mimic traditional pasta best, but if you prefer a heartier bite, experiment with a slightly thicker cut—just keep it consistent.

Keep the pan hot. A hot skillet ensures the noodles get a quick sear, preserving texture and preventing sogginess.

FAQ

Can I freeze mandoline zucchini noodles?

Yes, but texture changes slightly after thawing. Freeze them on a baking sheet in a single layer, then transfer to a freezer bag. Reheat directly in a hot skillet; they’ll regain some firmness.

Do I need to peel zucchini before slicing?

Peeling is optional. The skin adds nutrients and color, but if you prefer a smoother noodle or have a thicker-skinned variety, peel it before using the Mandoline Slicer.

Is the Mandoline Slicer safe for beginners?

Absolutely. The built‑in hand guard protects fingers, and the adjustable blades let you start with a thicker cut until you’re comfortable. Just follow the safety instructions, and you’ll get perfect ribbons quickly.
